text.title: subagent-as-context-firewall Failure Modes
text.summary: 6 antipatterns specific to subagent-as-context-firewall. Each has a description, an observable detector and a concrete repair.

failure-mode.description: Subagent returns 50K tokens of everything it found: file bodies, quoted paragraphs, full diffs, inside the `summary` field or an extra free-form field.
failure-mode.detector: Returned contract exceeds 500 tokens, or contains code fences / multi-line quotes, or the contract model has a string field without a length validator. Parent context grows by more than 1K per subagent call.
failure-mode.repair: Close the contract to `summary`, `refs`, `confidence`, `next_actions`; set `max_tokens` on the call and a length validator on `summary`; move evidence to `refs`. Rules r-slim-contract-mandatory, r-summary-token-cap, r-refs-over-content.

failure-mode.description: Parent re-passes one subagent's output to another subagent, or into its own next turn, without slimming: raw transcripts are concatenated and forwarded.
failure-mode.detector: A subagent prompt contains another subagent's tool results or transcript verbatim; the gather step's input size equals the sum of the subagents' internal reading rather than the sum of their contracts.
failure-mode.repair: Forward the contract object or its `refs` only; each boundary slims. Rule r-no-unslimmed-passthrough.

failure-mode.description: A subagent is spawned for a question one direct file read would answer: the overhead (system prompt, contract, round-trip) costs more than the reading.
failure-mode.detector: The task brief names a single known file or a single tool call, no untrusted input, and the subagent finishes in one or two tool calls.
failure-mode.repair: Read the file directly in the parent. Reserve the firewall for many reads, unknown locations or untrusted input; the decision tree's first question is this threshold.

failure-mode.description: Multiple subagents share state through a shared conversation or a copied parent transcript, so one sibling's reading lands in all of them.
failure-mode.detector: The subagent invocation passes the parent's message history or another subagent's messages as input; parallel subagents' token usage is correlated instead of independent.
failure-mode.repair: Fresh window per invocation with only brief + contract + tool list; coordinate through files on disk. Rule r-fresh-window-per-invocation.

failure-mode.description: Subagent crash or timeout swallows the parent's question: the parent receives an exception, `None` or an empty string and proceeds as if nothing was asked.
failure-mode.detector: Parent code has no `except` around the subagent call, or the exception handler returns `None`; logs show a subagent timeout with no corresponding low-confidence report.
failure-mode.repair: Always return a contract with `confidence: "low"`, a summary naming the failure and a retry suggestion in `next_actions`. Rule r-structured-failure.

failure-mode.description: Attacker-controlled text (web page, upload, email) is read directly in the parent, or in a subagent that still has shell, write or network tools.
failure-mode.detector: A fetch / read of external content appears in the parent transcript; or the sandbox subagent's tool list includes anything beyond reading its input; or the extraction schema has a free-text field that echoes the source.
failure-mode.repair: Route the input through a no-tool subagent with a fixed extraction schema whose system prompt names the source as untrusted; parent treats the fields as data. Rule r-untrusted-input-wrapped.
